Secondly, keeping the blinds down helps to regulate cabin temperature. Sunlight streaming in can significantly increase the internal temperature of the aircraft, which could lead to discomfort for passengers and complicate the cabin crew's job. Thirdly, it ensures that passengers are not overly distracted by the view outside, particularly during critical phases of the flight, allowing everyone to focus on safety instructions and messages from the crew. Lastly, it promotes a more uniform experience for all passengers, minimizing glare from the sun, which can be particularly bothersome on longer flights. So, the next time you hear the crew request that the blinds be closed, remember it’s all about ensuring a safer and more comfortable flying experience for everyone on board!
